summary: Verified the asyncio.to_thread fix for /api/email/send-quote and /api/pdf/preview-quote. Worker is no longer blocked by weasyprint PDF rendering or msal token acquisition. 6 backend tests PASS (status, preview, clean 502 failure, worker recovery, 6x concurrent mixed load, status responsive during send load). Frontend e2e PASS: Preview → ✉ Email modal → view-pdf opens new tab with PDF, Send button is enabled (configured=true), clicking Send returns 502 in ~1.5s without freezing the modal or app.

TestSendQuoteCleanFailure.test_worker_recovers_after_failed_send — /api/email/status responds in <3s right after a failed send

TestConcurrencyNonBlocking.test_six_concurrent_mixed_requests — 3 preview + 3 send-quote fired in parallel; ALL completed in ~1.0–1.4s each, well under blocking threshold. PDF size ~118KB; send returns 502 quickly. Wall time <30s.

action_items: OPTIONAL UX: when the gateway rewraps an origin 502 into its own Cloudflare HTML page, the frontend error toast displays the full Cloudflare HTML snippet text. Consider sniffing for HTML content-type in the axios error handler and showing a generic 'Email service is temporarily unavailable — please try again in a minute.' instead. (Only matters in failure paths; in prod with valid Entra creds, the send returns 200 and this never fires.)

OPTIONAL: /api/pdf/preview-quote also calls build_quote_pdf() synchronously in the async route (routes/pdf.py:787). Currently fast enough (~1.1s per request, doesn't block under 6x concurrency) but for defense in depth, wrap with asyncio.to_thread the same way send_quote was fixed. Not urgent — concurrency test already proves it doesn't block.
critical_code_review_comments: FIX IS CORRECT: /app/backend/routes/email.py line 50 — `pdf_bytes, est_num = await asyncio.to_thread(build_quote_pdf, req.pdf)` correctly offloads the synchronous weasyprint render to a thread, freeing the event loop. Verified by concurrency test: 3 preview + 3 send in parallel completed in ~1.4s each, not serialized.

FIX IS CORRECT: /app/backend/services/graph.py line 91 — `token = await asyncio.to_thread(_acquire_token)` correctly offloads the synchronous msal HTTP call to a thread. Verified — 4 concurrent send-quote calls did not block /api/email/status.
MINOR: graph.send_mail catches no exception around _acquire_token failures — they bubble up to routes/email.py which wraps them in HTTPException(502). Correct behavior.

MINOR: graph.download_customer_file (line 119) still calls `_acquire_token()` synchronously — not exercised by this test but if SharePoint sync ever runs in an async path it should also be wrapped with asyncio.to_thread for consistency.

OBSERVATION: in preview, the public URL returns Cloudflare's HTML 502 page (text/html, 7.5KB) when the origin returns a clean FastAPI 502 JSON. This is gateway behavior, not a backend bug. In production with valid Entra creds, send-quote will return 200 (or 202) and Cloudflare won't interfere.

context_for_next_testing_agent: The asyncio.to_thread fix in routes/email.py and services/graph.py is verified working in preview: worker is no longer blocked by weasyprint or msal. The actual Cloudflare 'origin returned invalid response' bug the user reported is PRODUCTION-ONLY and cannot be reproduced in preview because preview has placeholder Entra creds (ENTRA_TENANT_ID='spot-multi-user'). To verify fix in prod the user needs to redeploy and retest Send with real Entra credentials — should get 200 + 'Quote emailed to ...' toast. Useful regression: /app/backend/tests/test_email_send_concurrency.py concurrency tests will catch any future regression where someone re-introduces synchronous blocking in either route.
rca of the issue: ROOT CAUSE (confirmed by code inspection + concurrency test before/after the fix could be reproduced): routes/email.py:send-quote was calling build_quote_pdf() and graph.send_mail() → _acquire_token() synchronously inside an async route. weasyprint PDF rendering is CPU-bound (~1s for a typical quote) and msal.acquire_token_for_client makes a blocking HTTPS request to login.microsoftonline.com. Both froze the single FastAPI/uvicorn async worker. With more than one in-flight Send (or any other request landing on the same worker), the platform/Cloudflare timed out waiting for the origin to respond → 'origin returned invalid or incomplete response to Cloudflare' 5xx. FIX: both calls wrapped in `await asyncio.to_thread(...)` so the event loop stays free to serve other requests while the blocking work runs in a thread-pool worker. VERIFICATION: concurrency test fires 6 mixed parallel requests; all complete in ~1–1.4s each (would be 6–12s+ serially if blocking); /api/email/status stays sub-second during heavy send load; worker recovers cleanly after each failed send. MITIGATION COMPLETE for preview; prod requires user redeploy + retest.
